title: With a stateless makeover, new MCP spec targets enterprise scale
gist: The Model Context Protocol's biggest update since launch converts its core from a bidirectional stateful protocol to stateless request/response, removing the session-affinity barrier that blocked enterprise-scale deployment of MCP servers. Governance sits with the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, but Anthropic-employed maintainers still steer direction even as OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Amazon contribute.

themes.theme: Stateless core removes the scaling ceiling

insights.claim: MCP's protocol core is now stateless, so requests no longer depend on a session tied to an individual server instance—the constraint that made horizontal scaling and load balancing of MCP servers hard.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Session affinity was the technical reason agentic tool-use stayed in pilots; removing it is a precondition for production enterprise agent deployments and the infra spend that follows.
insights.quote: MCP is transforming from a bidirectional stateful protocol into a request/response stateless protocol.
insights.locator: The blog post announcing the specification

insights.claim: The maintainers say statelessness was one of the most highly requested features from developers seeking better reliability and scalability, indicating demand was already bottlenecked on infrastructure rather than model capability.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Signals that the binding constraint on agent adoption in 2026 is plumbing, not intelligence—favoring infra and integration vendors over model providers on the margin.
insights.quote: It was one of the most highly-requested features from developers who were eager to get better reliability and scalability for their MCP servers.
insights.locator: The highlight of this release is a stateless protocol core

insights.claim: The release also adds Multi Round-Trip Requests, header-based routing, cacheable list results, authorization hardening, a formal extensions framework, and updated Tier 1 SDKs—a feature set aimed squarely at CDN-style and enterprise deployment patterns.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Header-based routing and cacheable results mean existing enterprise network infrastructure can front MCP traffic—lowering the cost of adoption for large IT estates.

insights.claim: MCP began as a local-machine protocol connecting models to local apps, so the new spec is a foundational rethink rather than an incremental version bump.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Early-standard architectural debt is being paid down now; expect breakage and migration work at firms that built on the stateful assumption.
insights.locator: MCP started as something that simply ran on a local machine

insights.claim: A new deprecation policy guarantees at least 12 months between a feature's formal deprecation and its actual removal, with a narrow carve-out for critical security updates.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Predictable deprecation windows are what procurement and platform teams need before betting roadmaps on a standard—an underappreciated adoption unlock.
insights.locator: There is also a new deprecation policy

insights.claim: Lead maintainer Soria Parra characterized this as MCP's most important update since remote MCP launched over a year ago.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Frames a dating milestone for the agentic-tooling stack: remote MCP is roughly one year old and only now production-shaped.
insights.quote: MCP’s most important since remote MCP first launched over a year ago

insights.claim: MCP is managed by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation, but Anthropic—which introduced it just under two years ago—still holds significant influence over its direction because principal maintainers work there.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: De jure neutrality with de facto vendor influence is the classic open-standard control pattern—Anthropic gets ecosystem legitimacy while retaining agenda-setting power.
insights.quote: The buck technically stops with individual maintainers, not any of these companies themselves, but as noted above, some of the principal maintainers currently work at Anthropic.
insights.locator: The buck technically stops with individual maintainers

insights.claim: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Amazon all contribute to MCP, meaning the major model and cloud providers have converged on a single tool-connection standard rather than fragmenting into rival protocols.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Standard convergence compresses integration costs and shifts competition to model quality and distribution—bad for anyone whose moat was proprietary connectors.
insights.locator: Nonetheless, it has grown beyond just Anthropic
